messages:
Anya (AE): Heads-up — Acme POC hitting intermittent 429s during bulk import demo. Started at ~09:12 PT. They send ~50 parallel embedding requests and ~15 completions calls. Can SRE triage?
Sam B. (SRE): On it. Do we have request ids or an example curl?
Anya (AE): Yep, customer pasted this curl + response: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -d '{\"input\": [..]}'` -> HTTP/1.1 429 {\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\"}
Maria S. (Solutions): Also seeing 4xx spikes in our dashboard at the same time window (09:11–09:14). Looks per-tenant, not global.
Lee (oncall): Pasting our internal rate_limiter log for tenant acme-123: `2026-03-21T16:11:22Z rate_limiter INFO reject tenant=acme-123 route=/v1/embeddings reason=burst_limit tokens=470 window=60s token_budget=500`
Lee (oncall): Another line: `2026-03-21T16:11:24Z rate_limiter DEBUG accounting double_count_detected tenant=acme-123 stream=true`
Sam B. (SRE): Interesting — logs show burst_limit hits and a double-count accounting flag. Could be streaming responses counted twice for token budget.
Maria S. (Solutions): The customer runs a client that opens one streaming completions per item + separate embedding calls. If streaming tokens are double-counted, their token_budget (500/min) will be exhausted quickly.
Anya (AE): Can we do a temporary quota bump to keep the demo going? They asked about pricing if we bump capacity.
Sam B. (SRE): We can grant a soft quota bump to 2000 token/min for the demo window. Need an internal ticket. Note: this won't fix the double-counting.
Sam B. (SRE): Quick mitigation: advise client to disable streaming for completions during the bulk import or batch embeddings into larger requests to reduce per-request overhead.
Maria S. (Solutions): Patch idea — set `stream=false` or use `batch_size=32` for embeddings. I'll send a short how-to snippet to the customer.
Lee (oncall): Creating infra ticket INF-4782 to track root cause (double-counting) and deploying a hotfix candidate to staging. QuotaBot: auto-generated note -> "Quota change request created for acme-123: +1500 tokens/min for 2 hours. Approver: finance@sales.redwood"
Anya (AE): Thanks — I'll loop in the customer and confirm they can switch to non-streaming for the demo. Also can you confirm whether the temporary bump is billable pro-rata?
Sam B. (SRE): Billing: temporary bump will be recorded as overage and billed; for enterprise demo exceptions we can approve a one-off credit (ping finance).
Maria S. (Solutions): Follow-up: adding dashboard panel for per-route token accounting and a trace link to the ticket: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/INF-4782
Anya (AE): Customer confirmed switching off streaming, demo recovered. Keeping thread open until fix verified in staging. :thumbsup:
Lee (oncall): Will post when hotfix candidate passes staging load test (ETA ~2h).
Sam B. (SRE): Root cause hypothesis: streaming path invoked both streaming and non-streaming accounting on some code paths -> double charge. Patch will dedupe accounting entries.
Anya (AE): Great, please notify me when hotfix deploys so I can tell Acme.
Maria S. (Solutions): Drafted short note for customer with rollback steps and temporary config. Sending after we confirm hotfix schedule.
EngInfra Bot: Deploy INF-4782-hotfix -> staging started at 2026-03-21T18:00:10Z
Lee (oncall): Staging passed 30m soak, no double-count logs now. Promoting to canary.
Anya (AE): Promoted to canary, Acme re-ran bulk import and saw zero 429s. They signed off on demo. Closing once canary to prod complete. :tada:
